entries.name: George Daniels

expected.charges: Advising/urging insubordination and refusal of duty; disloyal statements
expected.sentence:
U.S. Marine convicted by court-martial for privately calling Vietnam a 'white man's war'; charged with advising, urging and attempting to cause insubordination, disloyalty and refusal of duty. Sentenced to about 10 years at hard labor (combined with William Harvey's term totaling ~16 years).

Verdict as recorded: Yes — convicted by court-martial (Dec. 1967)

updates.sentence:
U.S. Marine convicted by court-martial for privately calling Vietnam a 'white man's war'; charged with advising, urging and attempting to cause insubordination, disloyalty and refusal of duty. Sentenced to about 10 years at hard labor (combined with William Harvey's term totaling ~16 years).

Verdict as recorded: Yes — convicted by court-martial (Dec. 1967)

Released pending appeal September 3, 1969. A contemporary Clergy and Laymen Concerned newsletter reports twenty-five months actually spent in prison. This reported duration supplies the counter; the exact initial confinement date remains unresolved, so the admission year is retained without an invented day or month.

entries.rationale: Contemporary CALCAV newsletter reproduced Congressional Record October14 1969 p29877 explicitly gives September3 release pending appeal and 25 months served. Existing December1967 admission conflates later court-martial chronology with earlier custody and is incompatible with the reported duration. Retain only 1967 precision; do not calculate an admission date backward from rounded months. Preserve biography.

entries.name: William Harvey

expected.sentence:
Black Marine convicted in December 1967 of 'disloyal statements' for privately opposing the Vietnam War. Sentenced to about 6 years (6 to 10 years) at hard labor, held at Camp Pendleton, for words alone.

Verdict as recorded: Yes — convicted by court-martial (Dec. 1967)
